title: A Letter for the Will Revisited
premise: Zephyrine Underhill, coroner of the fading town of Marrow's Bend, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder listed in a decades-old will's codicil 'has not yet occurred' — a legal riddle that only makes sense when she realizes the codicil names her own family's gravesite as the future crime scene. As she digs into the Underhill inheritance she never claimed, she discovers the client is the estranged daughter of the woman whose body should be in that grave, and that someone has been maintaining the case file for thirty years, updating it like a living document. The killer is the town's beloved probate clerk, who has been quietly murdering his way through the inheritance line and rewriting the record to make each death look natural; the statute expires in nine days, and the file says Zephyrine is next. She stages her own death to draw him into the graveyard, traps him with the very documentation he perfected, and in the end chooses love over duty by letting the heiress — the woman she has come to care for — keep the fortune built on lies, burning the confession that would have undone them both.
about_author: Lena Halloran is the pen name of a former rural records clerk who spent eleven years filing probate documents in three counties and never stopped wondering which ones were lies. She writes mysteries where the paperwork is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A pale, precise stranger named Ivy Lark hires Zephyrine to prove a murder 'hasn't happened yet,' producing a will codicil dated 1994 that describes a death at the Underhill plot with unsettling detail. Zephyrine, who prides herself on closable cases, takes the retainer half out of pride, half because the codicil names her grandmother. Beat: uneasy curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She walks Marrow's Bend cemetery at dawn, matching the codicil's details against real stones, and finds one grave — her grandmother's — with fresh-turned earth beneath thirty years of moss. Ivy reveals the codicil predicts a murder that the town's records say never occurred. Beat: the ground itself becomes a suspect; Zephyrine's professional certainty cracks.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Never Retires
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Ivy Lark, revealed as the daughter of the codicil's author, searches probate archives and notices every inheritance death in the Underhill line was certified by the same man: probate clerk Ambrose Pell, who has held office for four decades and remembers everything. Beat: quiet paranoia — Ivy realizes she's being watched through the archive window.

chapters.title: A File That Breathes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She requests the Underhill case file and finds it impossibly current — pages added last month, her own name entered under 'anticipated parties.' Someone with legal access is maintaining the file as a living document. Pell is charming over tea and knows too much about her childhood. Beat: hunted feeling; the hunter realizes she is listed as prey.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Zephyrine and Ivy compare notes over cheap wine, and attraction tangles with distrust — Ivy has been lying about when she arrived in town. They admit the codicil's 'murder not yet occurred' clause was a dead woman's insurance: her way of forcing an investigation from beyond the grave. Beat: tenderness sharpened by betrayal; the first kiss happens over evidence.

chapters.title: Nine Days to Statute
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The statute of limitations on the original crime expires in nine days, after which the codicil's trigger dies and Pell walks free forever. Zephyrine reconstructs his method: he kills heirs, then amends records so the deaths postdate the will's expiry. The file lists her as the last Underhill. Beat: cold resolve; she stops investigating and starts planning.

chapters.title: What the Dead Woman Ordered
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Ivy decodes her mother's codicil fully: it names Pell as executor and requires the coroner to 'witness the grave' — a trap her mother built, betting a future coroner would read it literally. Ivy confesses she came to Marrow's Bend to finish her mother's plan, using Zephyrine. Beat: guilt and forgiveness; the two women choose each other and the case together.

chapters.title: The Staged Grave
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine fakes her own death — a falsified coroner's report filed through a deputy she trusts — and lies in the reopened Underhill grave as bait, knowing Pell must amend the record personally to make her death 'natural.' Ivy watches from the yew tree. Beat: terror held still; the town's quietest man approaches with a shovel.

chapters.title: Codicil and Claw
chapters.summary: Dual POV, climax. Pell opens the grave; Zephyrine rises and Ivy steps out with a recorder running as Pell, unravelling, confesses to four murders across forty years, believing the statute protects him — not knowing Zephyrine's staged death reactivated the codicil's clause, extending the clock. The deputy arrives with the warrant. Beat: cathartic reversal — the file's perfection becomes the noose.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Will, Revisited
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, resolution. Pell is convicted; the inheritance passes to Ivy, the last honest heir. Zephyrine burns her unofficial confession notes — duty satisfied by the court, but love protected by silence — and adds her grandmother's real headstone inscription, which reads 'Ask the right question twice.' She and Ivy plant something living over the grave. Beat: peace earned at a moral price; love chosen over the letter of the law.
